source_reviews.independent_solution: Let O have coordinate 0. If x_A=x_B, A=B, so |AB|=0=|x_B-x_A|. For x_A<x_B: when 0<=x_A<x_B, OB=OA+AB, so |AB|=x_B-x_A; when x_A<x_B<=0, OA=OB+AB, so |AB|=(-x_A)-(-x_B)=x_B-x_A; when x_A<0<x_B, O is between the endpoints and |AB|=|AO|+|OB|=-x_A+x_B=x_B-x_A. An endpoint at 0 is covered by the first two cases. Thus for x_A<=x_B the length is x_B-x_A=|x_B-x_A|. For x_A>x_B, interchange A and B to obtain |AB|=x_A-x_B=|x_B-x_A|. This covers all coordinate orders, signs and coincidence; the result is an unsigned length rather than a directed difference.
